introduction: ERC-5219 defines a read-only contract interface, IDecentralizedApp, that lets clients request resources from a smart contract and receive HTTP-like responses. It was proposed by Gavin John in July 2022. A caller invokes request() with a resource path split into segments and a list of query parameters, and the contract returns an HTTP status code, a response body, and response headers. Because request() is a view function, it needs no transaction, so a front-end can be served directly from on-chain code.
designPurpose: ERC-5219 was designed to remove the centralized web server that most decentralized apps still depend on for their user interface. When a front-end is hosted on an ordinary website it can be censored, taken down, or silently altered, and other contracts cannot read it. By specifying a single view function that returns a status code, body, and headers, ERC-5219 lets an interface live on-chain, so it can be fetched trustlessly, is as permanent as the contract itself, and can be read by other smart contracts.
commonUsage: ERC-5219 is used by projects that publish a fully on-chain front-end alongside their application logic, and by gateway software that translates ordinary web requests into request() calls so a browser can load the result. To keep gas costs low, implementers often return a message/external-body response that points at content on IPFS instead of storing large assets on-chain. The interface pairs naturally with interface detection, letting clients discover which contracts speak the protocol.
fn.request.desc: Sends an HTTP GET-like request for a resource and returns an HTTP-style response. The resource path is passed as an array of segments and the query string as key/value pairs; the function is view, so it never changes state.
fn.request.params.resource: The requested resource path split into segments, so that "/asdf/1234" becomes ["asdf", "1234"].
fn.request.params.params: The query parameters as key/value pairs, so that "?foo=bar" becomes [{ key: "foo", value: "bar" }].
fn.request.returns.statusCode: The HTTP status code of the response, such as 200 for success or 404 when the resource is not found.
fn.request.returns.body: The body of the response, for example an HTML document or JSON payload.
fn.request.returns.headers: A list of response headers as key/value pairs, such as Content-Type.
sim.requestWalkthrough.name: Resource Request Walkthrough
sim.requestWalkthrough.desc: Follow a request() call from the client through the contract to the HTTP-like response it returns.
sim.requestWalkthrough.step.call: The client calls request() on the DApp contract, passing the resource path and query parameters.
sim.requestWalkthrough.step.resolve: The contract resolves the path and reads the matching content from its resource store.
sim.requestWalkthrough.step.build: The contract assembles an HTTP-like response with a status code, body, and headers.
sim.requestWalkthrough.step.return: The response is returned to the client, which renders it just like a normal web page.
